No matter what ontological status we assign to the action, the nonexistent agent cannot perform it. Nothingness cannot act upon anything.","quantum":"Just as the vacuum state in QFT cannot spontaneously produce forbidden processes (baryon number violation, etc.), inherent non-existence cannot produce any type of action. The logical constraints are as absolute for non-existence as for existence.","bridge":"Both physics and logic place absolute constraints on \"nothing.\" The vacuum cannot violate conservation laws; inherent non-existence cannot perform actions. Zero interacting with anything still yields zero.","accessible":"A ghost (nonexistent agent) can't build a ghost house (unreal action), a real house (cross-level), or a house that's both real and ghost (contradiction). Nothing cannot do anything — not even nothing.","twoTruths":"Conventionally, agents are not \"nothing\" — they exist dependently. The comprehensive elimination applies only to INHERENTLY nonexistent agents, showing nihilism is as unworkable as eternalism.","commonMisconception":"NOT saying agents don't exist. Saying INHERENTLY nonexistent agents (absolute nothingness) can't perform ANY type of action.
